title: Lord, Send Thy Word, and Let It Run
description: Lord, Send Thy Word, and Let It Run in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Gibbons wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 808 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Universal Peace”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, send thy word, and let it run, Armed with thy Spirit's po-wer; Ten thou-sand shall con-fess its sway, And bless the sa-ving hour.

lines: Lord, send thy word, and let it run,
Armed with thy Spirit's power;
Ten thousand shall confess its sway,
And bless the saving hour.
Beneath the influence of thy grace
The barren wastes shall rise,
With sudden greens and fruits arrayed,
A blooming paradise.
True holiness shall strike its root
In each regenerate heart,
Shall in a growth divine arise,
And heavenly fruits impart.
Peace, with her olives crowned, shall stretch
Her wings from shore to shore;
No trump shall rouse the rage of war,
Nor murderous cannon roar.
Lord, for those days we wait; — those days
Are in thy word foretold;
Fly swifter, sun and stars, and bring
This promised age of gold!

licence: Public domain: Thomas Gibbons died in 1785.
credits: Words by Thomas Gibbons (1720–1785), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
